gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured figure for how much power a station uses with its AC outlet on and nothing plugged in. With a 24–50 W reptile heater, that draw cuts runtime far more than ChatGPT's flat 85% efficiency assumes. The Technology Man measured about 19 W on the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2. The Solar Lab measured 16 W on the Elite 100 V2 and 9.5 W on the Elite 200 V2, plus 94% efficiency on the Elite 200 V2.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited, animalstart.com (smart-thermostat article) and pets.co.uk (vivarium winter article), and the runtime tables ChatGPT built. AnimalStart gives one rough estimate ('100W heater ... about 5 hours on a 500Wh battery') and names Jackery and Goal Zero with no specs. Pets.co.uk gives a Wh ÷ W formula with no numbers and names no power station. Neither page has an idle-draw, usable-capacity or transfer-time measurement. All three ChatGPT answers use one flat 85% factor and never count the inverter's own draw. That draw is two-thirds of a 24 W heat mat's load on a 1 kWh unit and nearly as large as the mat on a 288 Wh unit. I could not open the rank-1 Petco page (HTTP 403).
decides: This confirms the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 as the pick for multi-day heat. It had the lowest measured idle draw (9.5 W, The Solar Lab) and the highest measured efficiency (94%, The Solar Lab; above 93%, about 2,000 Wh, The Gadgeteer). By my arithmetic it keeps a 24 W mat going for roughly 2,073.6 × 0.93 ÷ (24 + 9.5) ≈ 57 h. It also demotes the 288–300 Wh units (Elite 30 V2, Tenergy T320) to 'a few hours only'. The Technology Man measured about 19 W of AC idle on the Elite 30 V2 with Eco mode off, and only 231 Wh usable on AC. That gives at most 288 ÷ (24 + 19) ≈ 6.7 h for a 24 W mat, the bottom-to-middle of our page's 'About 6–8 h', and about 288 ÷ (50 + 19) ≈ 4.2 h for a 100 W emitter at half duty. Shoppers should also be told to turn off Eco/auto-off for AC: it cuts idle draw but can shut the outlet off while the thermostat has the heater switched off. For the 1 kWh class, The Solar Lab's 16 W idle on the Elite 100 V2 limits a 24 W mat to about 1,024 ÷ (24 + 16) ≈ 25.6 h. That supports 'about a day' as an upper bound, not a typical figure.
